question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}xy\,dx+yz\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the line $r(t)=t\,i+5t\,j+\,k$ for $t\in [2,3]?$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)=5t,\,z(t)=1.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,k \\  & =\,i+5\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+yz\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{2}^{3}xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+yz\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+yz\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}5{t}^{2}\cdot (1)+5t\cdot (5)+1\cdot (0)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}5{t}^{2}+25t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
